Figure 2:Overview of the Ent-Dataset.(a)Ent-Syn pipeline:source robot trajectories undergo (1) keyframe hand editing, (2) motion-guided video generation, and (3) VLM verification for visual quality and action consistency, before pairing the generated human video with the original robot observations and actions.
(b)Dataset composition:concentric rings (from inner to outer) break down all 21,269 paired episodes by data source (Ent-Real, Astribot, AgiBot), human-video source (Human, Seedance, Wan), train/validation split (19,115 / 2,154), and task category (635 tasks).
(c)Paired demonstrations:examples from the Ent-Real and Ent-Syn subsets across five matched timestamps, illustrating temporally aligned robot and human executions.

Figure 3:Overview of Entangle.(a) Human context and the current robot observation condition joint
video–action prediction, with action tokens attending to video tokens.
(b) Temporal RoPE places context and robot video sequentially while
preserving local spatial coordinates, and anchors action positions to
the robot segment.
(c) Each inference round jointly denoises future video and actions,
executes an action prefix, and replans with updated observations and
context.

Figure 4:Six real-robot tasks with execution frames in chronological order.
The cyan arrow in (f) marks the required left opening.

Figure 6:Four types of Context-OOD, shown as compact process sequences. (a) Pen placement with changed spatial layout;
selected frames show the initial scene and the first two placements.
(b) Black-to-white mouse substitution: lines denote mouse
writing strokes.
(c) Picture-frame-to-stand transfer preserves the hold-and-wipe
interaction. (d) A banana takes the unconventional role of a sweeping
tool.

Figure 7:Cloth rotation and toss in two rollouts conditioned on the same human video. Schematic arrows show circular or side-to-side motion during the turning phase and the toss or drop direction in the final column. The cloth color differs across the rollouts.
Figure 8:Circles mark the frame snag (middle row) and early left-gripper withdrawal (bottom row).

Figure 9:Deployment from Seedance-generated context without a recorded
human demonstration. Astribot S1 first pushes the pen holder, then gathers
three pens. Yellow arrows indicate motion.
Figure 10:The robot reproduces the demonstrated handover motions on an empty tabletop.

Figure 11:Human demonstrations and robot executions for the six real-robot tasks.
Each row shows early and late demonstration frames, followed by initial, intermediate, and late frames from the robot head camera.
